title: AnchorBoard: Contextual batching & caching guidance surface
creator: Ava Rodriguez
description: Create an interactive guidance surface called AnchorBoard inside the Redwood Console that surfaces model-aware batching and prefix/KV-cache recommendations, explains trade-offs, and offers safe default guardrails. The surface will appear as a docked panel on the Route & Model config page and provide: 1) a concise recommendation card with expected cost savings and latency impact; 2) a small workload simulator that replays representative request traces; 3) an explainability ribbon showing why a recommendation was chosen (e.g., high prefix reuse, short prompt tails); and 4) quick toggles to apply presets (conservative, aggressive, experimental) with rollbackable canary policies for rollout. Design must balance simplicity for new users and direct controls for platform engineers (advanced mode).
acceptance_criteria: AnchorBoard prototype created in Figma with screens for empty state, recommended preset, simulator playback, and preset application flow
Prototype shows estimated token-savings, p50/p95 latency delta, and confidence band for quality regression risk
UX flows for applying a preset, scheduling a canary rollout, and automatic fallback are documented and linked to PRD
Design review feedback from Product and Eng incorporated or explicitly documented as deferred
Handoff-ready spec with component-level tokens, microcopy, and accessibility notes in Confluence

comments: 2026-02-10 Ava Rodriguez: Initial ticket created. Rationale: customers confuse batching/caching controls and often over-tune without visibility. Goal is to reduce misconfigurations and shrink token spend by making recommendations actionable.

2026-02-15 Liam Patel: Completed wireframes. Pushed Figma draft: figma.com/file/REDWOOD/AnchorBoard-draft (private). Key question for Eng: can runtime provide per-route prefix-reuse estimate (samples/day) and a non-blocking cost delta estimate?

2026-02-18 Marcus Ng (eng): We can surface sample-based prefix reuse and a simulated per-token cost delta. p95 latency delta is best-effort; will be delivered as 'simulated' until runtime telemetry is extended.
2026-02-22 Rhea Chen (PM): Reviewed wireframes. Ask: clearly mark experimental presets and require explicit opt-in. Also request a lightweight audit entry to track preset applications for compliance.
2026-02-28 Design critique: PM/Eng asked to reduce cognitive load in empty state. Decided to combine explainer and one-click 'Analyze workload' CTA instead of multiple CTAs.

2026-03-03 Ava: Built mid-fidelity prototype showing three presets: conservative (safe), efficiency (balanced), throughput (aggressive). Prototype includes 'Why this recommendation' panel with bullet reasons and confidence score.

2026-03-06 Marcus Ng: Noted trade-off: aggressive preset cannot be rolled back automatically if it triggers quality regressions; runtime will provide alerting but manual rollback required for now. We flagged automatic rollback as an engineering spike (ENG-4219).
2026-03-09 UX review: Accessibility pass required on color contrast for confidence band. Also add ARIA live region for simulator playback updates.

2026-03-12 Liam: Incorporated feedback and uploaded final prototype and handoff pages. PRD updated with rollout gating logic and fallback policy examples: confluence.company.com/display/INF/AnchorBoard+PRD
2026-03-12 Rhea Chen: Approved to move to engineering handoff pending runtime telemetry stub endpoint availability. Due date proposed 2026-03-20.
decisions: Expose three presets only; advanced mode exposes individual knobs (batch size, max wait ms, prefix persistency TTL) to reduce surface area for most users
Simulator will operate on sampled traces (90s playback cap) to keep compute costs low
Experimental preset must show explicit 'opt-in' modal and create an audit log entry
Automatic rollback deferred; will include automated monitoring and alerting with manual rollback UI for initial release
